tools.why: Turns an office document (doc/docx/odt and friends) under the cursor into a picture in the hover window instead of a plain format badge — the conversion runs through pdfport.nvim's soffice producer. On Windows and macOS the LibreOffice installer does not extend PATH; `paths` below covers the default install location on both, so this only still reports missing on a genuinely atypical install (add the LibreOffice `program` directory to PATH yourself then, or `:Hover office off` to stop asking).

Renders a hovered http(s) link as a picture of the page, instead of previewing it as text — `:Hover links web shot` turns it on, and it is off by default because a render *executes* the page rather than downloading it. Any Chromium-based browser answers: chrome, chromium, brave or msedge, searched in that order. Not on PATH is the normal case rather than the exception — measured on Windows, the Chrome installer does not extend PATH at all. `paths` below covers the default per-user and system-wide install locations on Windows/macOS/Linux (the same list `hover/preview/shot.lua`'s own resolver uses at runtime), so this only still reports missing on a genuinely atypical install; `links.shot.command` names one outright. Same problem `soffice` above describes.

Renders the first page of a PDF under the cursor as the hover preview, rather than reporting it as bytes. Ships with poppler and is reached through pdfport.nvim — both have to be present, `:checkhealth hover` says which is missing.

Lifts a still out of a video under the cursor, so a .mp4 shows a frame in the hover window instead of a size in bytes — and the paging keys then step through the file. Reached through media.nvim, which also needs ffprobe from the same install to read the duration a percentage offset is taken of; both come from one package. On Windows, winget and scoop extend the *user* PATH, which a terminal started before the install does not have — media.nvim probes both shim directories itself, and `:checkhealth media` says what it found.
